skill.displayName: QR Code Generation And Recognition - 二维码生成识别

version.changelog:
- Initial release of the jisu-qrcode skill.
- Supports generating QR code images (base64 output) from text, with options for color, error correction level, template, and logo.
- Supports recognizing/decoding QR code contents from URLs or base64 images.
- Can fetch sample QR code templates.
- Requires JISU_API_KEY environment variable for use.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: jisu-qrcode
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is a standard wrapper for the Jisu Data QR code API (api.jisuapi.com). It implements generation, recognition, and template retrieval functionality using the Python 'requests' library. The code correctly handles the API key via environment variables and contains no signs of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: Skill mostly matches its stated QR-code API purpose, but there are small incoherences (script path mismatch, undeclared Python dependency) and it will transmit user content to a third-party API — review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required env (JISU_API_KEY), and code all target the Jisu QRCode API — the credential requested is appropriate for this purpose. Minor mismatch: SKILL.md shows the script path as 'skill/qrcode/qrcode.py' while the package contains 'qrcode.py' at repository root; this will cause runtime confusion but does not indicate malicious intent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions and the Python script only call the external API (https://api.jisuapi.com/qrcode) and do not read other system files or unrelated env vars. However, the skill will transmit whatever text, URLs, or image base64 the user provides to a third-party service — that includes potentially sensitive data. The README/examples send parameters (including logo URLs or base64 images) as GET params, which may expose large data in query strings or leak metadata. This network transmission to an external service is expected for the stated function but is a privacy/security consideration the user should understand.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) and no downloads, which lowers risk. One practical inconsistency: the script imports the 'requests' Python package but the manifest/metadata doesn't declare it or provide an install step. That will cause runtime failure on systems without requests installed and may confuse users.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only JISU_API_KEY is required and is the correct credential for calling the Jisu API. No unrelated environment variables or other service credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills, and has no install-time persistence behavior. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but is not combined with other high-risk privileges here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill legitimately calls the Jisu QRCode API and needs your JISU_API_KEY; that is expected. Before installing: (1) confirm you trust the Jisu API service and its privacy policy because the skill will send any provided text, URLs, or image base64 to api.jisuapi.com; avoid sending sensitive secrets or personal data. (2) Ensure Python's 'requests' package is available on the agent environment (the skill imports requests but doesn't declare installing it). (3) Fix the script path mismatch in SKILL.md or call the correct file location (examples reference skill/qrcode/qrcode.py but the file is qrcode.py at root) to avoid runtime errors. If you need stronger assurance, request the maintainer to: include a proper install spec that declares Python dependencies, correct the file path in documentation, and document how the API handles uploaded content.
